notes: Synced decks now line up on the kick. Liveolator was placing a track's first beat by looking at the whole drum mix, which on kick-and-hat music can land on the off-beat instead - two synced decks could sit a third of a beat apart, and a blend would flam. The beat grid is now found from the bass band, where the kick actually is.

When Liveolator cannot prove where a track's beat sits, it now matches the tempo without forcing the beats together, instead of locking confidently to the wrong place. A grid it cannot vouch for is treated as unknown rather than assumed good.
Every track is re-analyzed once on the next scan to pick up the improved beat grid. Tracks you have corrected by hand keep your correction.
Exported mixes keep their stereo image. Any track whose BPM already matched the set tempo was being rendered in mono - on a 68-minute test mix that was eleven minutes of it, with no warning.
Correcting a track's BPM or beat grid by hand no longer throws away the detected kick positions, so the deck can still snap to a real kick afterwards.

A track whose file is offline - a disconnected drive, or a OneDrive file that has not been downloaded - is now skipped by background analysis instead of being marked as failed. It used to have its BPM, key, cue points and structure erased when the file could not be read.
A failed analysis never discards the analysis a track already had. Only a successful one replaces it.

An AI agent can now build a whole set from your library: it picks tracks that mix in key and tempo, beat-matches them to one tempo, and renders preview audio of each transition so you can hear the blend before you play it.
Every track's structure - intro, builds, drops, outro - is now detected inside Liveolator, with no extra download needed.
Key detection is far more accurate. A flaw in the chroma analysis made most tracks collapse onto the same few keys; on a real test library correct keys went from 2 in 10 to 8 in 10.
Fixed tracks whose tempo read half again too fast - a 125 BPM track that came out as 168 now reads 125.
Scanning a folder now touches only that folder instead of re-walking your whole library, so a small rescan takes seconds instead of an hour.
You can now correct a track's BPM or key by hand and have that correction survive every later scan.
New DJ PRO tab: the whole mixer, both decks and the effect knobs on one screen with no scrolling, for when you want density over comfort.
SYNC now refuses to lock onto a beat grid it is not confident about, instead of quietly drifting a few bars later.
Import your library from Rekordbox, Traktor, VirtualDJ, Serato, Mixxx or Engine DJ - tracks, cue points, beat grids, keys and playlists come across.
Per-stem gain knobs on the DJ PRO decks, so you can pull the vocal or the drums down without touching the EQ.
This build also carries the beat-grid, waveform-scroll and CMD STUDIO 2A jog fixes announced with 0.6.0.
Live BPM counters now track a synced follower when you change the leader's tempo - no more frozen counter after SYNC.
Half/double-time beatmatches (e.g. 140 vs 70) read as matched, with a small half/double tag next to the BPM readout.
SYNC shows a clear "can't sync" state when two tracks are more than +/-15 percent apart, instead of doing nothing silently.
Library Play now auditions the selected track immediately on Deck A and counts it as a play.
Stem decks (experimental): right-click a track and choose "Separate stems" to split it into drums / bass / vocals / other, then turn on Stem decks in Settings to mute each stem live on either deck.
Stem separation runs offline (it needs the Advanced analysis engine) and takes a few minutes per track - prepare tracks before your set.
Stability and audio-engine fixes.
Built-in mixer effects: the channel FX button now adds a Moog-style low-pass filter, phaser, and reverb - no plugins needed.
Continuous beat-sync: SYNC holds a live tempo and phase lock with an on-screen lock indicator (BEAT SYNC v2).
Smarter automatic hot-cue placement on analyzed tracks.
Stability and audio-engine fixes throughout.
Maintenance build: fixes and small improvements.
Top status bar reorganized: the master limiter is centred under a MASTER label, the computer volume is separated and relabelled SYS VOL, and the controls are one consistent size.
More DJ library imports: Serato, VirtualDJ, Mixxx and Engine DJ join Rekordbox and Traktor — tracks, hot cues, beat grids, key and playlists/crates.
Set the downbeat: place bar "one" exactly on the grid and waveform, with smarter downbeat handling.
Jog or seek on one deck no longer disturbs the other playing deck.
Each deck shows its live BPM, with a highlight when the two decks are matched.
Folded "butterfly" waveform and DJ mixer layout polish.
Closing the window can no longer freeze the app on exit.
Clearer load errors, transport stays disabled until a track is loaded, and hot cues are auto-placed on load.
SYNC is no longer silently starved when a track's BPM is missing from the catalog.
New vintage scalloped knob themes for the Retro Sci-Fi look.
First alpha build available to download from this site.
Library import from Rekordbox (XML) and Traktor (NML) - tracks, cues, grids, key and playlists.
Hot cue management across the libraries and the decks.
Beat-detection accuracy overhaul (kick-onset detection, downbeat estimation, beat grid).
Smart master limiter with adaptive, program-dependent release.
Early internal alpha build.
NUDGE is now a momentary pitch-bend for manual beat-matching.
First internal alpha installer.
